alternatives.argument: Define compactness of the weak closure, weakly convergent subsequences, and indexed weak cluster points, with relative limits in X and absolute limits in A. Haase Appendix E.5 printed pp353–354 states these distinctions. A cluster means every neighborhood meets arbitrarily late terms, including eventually constant sequences; the empty set satisfies all relative forms. No theorem from the unavailable Whitley text is used.

Haase Appendix E.1/E.5 gives a complete alternate proof. Alaoglu makes K=B_X* weak-star compact Hausdorff; Hahn–Banach makes x↦(f↦f(x)) an isometric weak-to-pointwise embedding Φ:X→C(K). Scalar boundedness from relative weak countable compactness and uniform boundedness give norm boundedness of A. Grothendieck E.14 is proved by embedding the pointwise closure of Φ(A) in a compact product of scalar disks (compact-Hausdorff Tychonoff) and showing each closure function g is continuous: if g fails continuity at y, recursively choose f_n∈Φ(A) close to g on y and earlier x_m and nested neighborhoods U_n of y whose closures control f_n; choose x_n∈U_n where g differs from g(y) by ε. A pointwise cluster f∈Φ(X) of f_n and compact cluster x of x_n force f(x)=g(y), f(x_m)=g(x_m), contradicting continuity of f. To put g back in Φ(X), use E.3: finite open covers of K^n yield a countable A0⊂A with g in its pointwise closure. Its closure is compact by E.14, separable by A0, and metrizable by E.2: a countable dense family on K induces a continuous pseudometric, countable finite nets yield evaluation points separating the compact closure (E.1 compact-cluster transfer). Hence a sequence from A0 converges pointwise to g. Relative weak countable compactness gives a weak cluster a∈X, so g=Φ(a) by uniqueness. Restrict any weak-star cluster x** of J(A) to K to obtain such a g, then scale to all X* to conclude x**=J(a). DC supplies countable recursive and finite-cover selections; The ultrafilter lemma supplies compactness and HB supplies norming.

The complete alternate countable-compactness lemma above gives bounded A and weak-star closure J(A)⊂J(X). Alaoglu makes that closure compact; J identifies it homeomorphically with the weak closure of A. Thus relative weak countable compactness implies relative weak compactness. Conversely, for a sequence in relatively weakly compact A, its closed separable span Y is weakly closed in X and has the inherited weak topology by Hahn–Banach. The compact weak closure of the sequence lies in Y and is weakly metrizable by the existing separable compact-metrization lemma; hence it has a weakly convergent subsequence. Relative sequential compactness trivially implies relative countable compactness. This proves all three equivalences for real and complex Banach spaces without invoking Whitley’s inaccessible induction.
